sector_model: fabless semiconductor, AI connectivity: revenue growth, gross margin, customer concentration, inventory and receivables build, SBC and dilution, EV/sales and P/E; no debt model
thesis: Astera Labs (Nasdaq: ALAB) sells high-speed connectivity chips (retimers, switches, controllers) plus COSMOS software to AI and cloud infrastructure customers. Q3 2026 10-Q (full financial statements, concentration and tax notes read) filed 2026-11-04. Q3 revenue 584.9M (+153.7% from 230.6M), nine months 1,285.7M (+120.9%); Q3 gross margin 72.3%, operating income 179.1M (30.6% margin). TTM revenue 1,556.2M, TTM GAAP net income 461.3M (tax benefit 48.1M in 9M26 lifted GAAP; pretax 9M 368.3M). Cash and marketable securities 1,378M, no borrowings, equity 2.0B. 9M OCF 341.5M after 347M working-capital build (receivables 284M vs 83M, inventory 201M vs 59M); capex 73.4M (+289%). TTM FCF about 345M. Close 230.91 on 2026-11-11 (+6.8% that day; +28.7% since 11-05 close 179.47). Market cap about 40.4B (174.78M shares at 10-31), EV about 39.0B: about 87x TTM GAAP earnings, 25x TTM sales, 0.85% FCF yield (0.27% after SBC). The business is high quality and growing very fast; the price already capitalizes years of continued hypergrowth.
counterthesis: At 25x sales and 87x earnings, any deceleration, a customer shifting to in-house or competitor silicon (Broadcom, Marvell, Credo), or lower AI capex would cut the multiple sharply. Customer A was 53% of Q3 revenue and 58% of receivables, and the 10-Q says concentration moves between manufacturing partners, so end-customer exposure is not fully visible. SBC is 195M in nine months (15% of revenue) with about 10M dilutive shares above basic; warrants issued to customers reduce revenue (30.4M) and signal pricing concessions. Working capital absorbed more than a third of net income plus SBC; inventory is 3.4x year-end. GAAP profit is helped by tax benefits and a valuation allowance that is still in place. Insider Forms 144 and 4 filed 11-05 and 11-09 (contents unread). The stock moved +29% in six sessions with no unread-evidence explanation, so the entry price embeds momentum. Peers and consensus are unknown to me. A director resigned 11-03.
invalidation: Revenue growth below about 50% year on year, gross margin below 70%, a top customer falling below 30% share without replacement, inventory and receivables growing faster than revenue for two quarters, or export-control restrictions on China-linked customers. A price decline to a multiple that peers justify would change the valuation view but not the quality view.
